items.title: Jimmy Witherspoon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, FL, April 12, 1996
items.q: Then that’s where I joined Jay McShann.

ctx.x: What kind of music was going on in your home?
Jimmy Lunceford, Count Basie, Benny Goodman, Artie Shaw, Andy Kirk, Jay McShann. Those kind of people you know.
Some of those people who you later on in life became pretty familiar with.

items.title: 52193_Jay McShann oral history interview
items.q: Spoon had been with me before those other guys. But I guess I kept them together about a year.

ctx.x: Blues Bailey. I'm trying to think of what was his first name. What was his first name? Max Bailey. Max "Blues" Bailey. And so he was supposed to join Charlie Barnet . And then I don't think he lasted over a few days with Charlie Barnet , because he had a pretty good drinking problem, and so Spoon was at the dance that night at Vallejo, California. So he says, hey, man, where's Brown? I told him - I'm trying to think, where was Brown then?

Well, Brown wasn't with the group. So I told him he wasn't with the group, and I -- he says, well, who you been having? I told him I'd been having Bailey and I told him Bailey was going with Barnet (inaudible). So, man, I think I can sing the blues. Let me do some blues with you. So he got up and sang some blues.

items.title: Jay McShann interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: We had a lot of fun... You had a big hand in his first recordings

ctx.x: Yeah? No kidding. My goodness. And Jimmy Witherspoon came on board a little bit later?
Yes, yes, Spoon came on board later. We had a lot of fun, yes sir. Yeah Spoon wanted to sing the blues. Yeah, he wanted to sing the blues.
You had a big hand in his first recordings, right? “Ain’t Nobody’s Business.”
